items.name: GPT-6 Cyber — OpenAI
items.summary: OpenAI is reportedly preparing to unveil GPT-6 Cyber at DevDay on Sep 29: a cybersecurity-focused model for enterprise AI deployment and automated vulnerability patching, currently in alpha with Daybreak Red program customers. If confirmed it would be the company's fourth cyber-specialized model of 2026.

items.name: Xing4.0-29B-A4B — China Telecom AI
items.summary: China Telecom AI released Xing4.0-29B-A4B, a 29B-parameter mixture-of-experts agentic model (4B active) for multi-step tool-calling workflows: 256K context, 75.0 on SWE-bench Verified, and deployable on a single GPU with just 15GB memory. Published on GitHub (XingChen-AGI) and Hugging Face.

items.name: CLM-8B — Stanford + NVIDIA
items.summary: Stanford and NVIDIA researchers released Contrastive Language Models, a new non-generative "decision model" approach for AI agents: CLM-8B (frozen Qwen3-8B backbone) ranks candidate actions instead of generating tokens, running up to 9x faster than TypeSafe's Jev in zero-shot tests. Weights are open under Apache 2.0; a multimodal CLM-35B-A3B is planned for early October.

items.name: LFM2.5-VL-3B-DSpark — Liquid AI
items.summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-VL-3B-DSpark, an experimental speculative-decoding draft model for its LFM2.5-VL-3B vision-language model: decoding up to 3.13x faster on Apple Silicon and 2.66x on NVIDIA H100 with identical output. Weights are live on Hugging Face (Safetensors + GGUF) with day-one SGLang, MLX-VLM, and llama.cpp support.

items.name: Tev1-4B-experimental — Together AI
items.summary: Together AI released Tev1-4B-experimental, a 4B "decision model" fine-tuned on Qwen3.5-4B that returns a single choice letter from structured state/question/options inputs — inspired by TypeSafe's Jev. Together also published a guide to training custom Jev-style classifiers for about $17.
